title: The decision record contract: one ledger of decisions of both kinds, with a state that never holds a table value, every answer, and labels from four sources
request: The owner asked for every decision and step to be stored as training data for decision models of any kind (open-source fine-tuned, classical, hosted like Jev), in two uses: for data scientists and inside DCLab's workflow.
spec: DecisionRecord v1 (point from one shared vocabulary, subject, state in bands, options, every answer, value used, level, ids) and DecisionLabel v1 (value, source benchmark/blind/user_decision_exposed/measured, who and when, supersedes, evidence) in dclab_core; adapters reading the main product's semantic_decision_answers and project_decision_records. Done when three kinds of decision round-trip, a state carrying a cell value is refused, and a main-product row becomes a record and back.
plan: Read the main product's Jev at the recorded commit: its bands, its purposes, its acting bands, its answer row and its decision records.
One vocabulary of points (technical and workflow), each naming the main product's governed point, Jev's purpose and the plan's key.
A state of declared fields only (Jev's bands where Jev has the field); answers, options and labels checked against the point's answer shape.
Adapters both ways for Jev's rows; decision records at their points from the facts their services write.

decisions.decision: The state is a closed vocabulary of typed fields, not free metadata.
decisions.why: It is what a decision model trains on: anything open could carry a row's value; Jev's own bands are reused so a model trained here answers there on the same inputs.

decisions.decision: Names are allowed in the state as stored.
decisions.why: A column's name is what Jev sends too (as untrusted text); refusing names would make the identifier and leakage points unanswerable. Counts and measures can only be aggregates by the caller's discipline: stated as a limit.

decisions.decision: A label row of the main product labels the decision at the root of its chain; it is never a second decision.
decisions.why: Its check constraint makes every label row supersede the row before it; reading it as a record duplicated decisions and pointed labels at ids that never existed.

decisions.decision: A blind label read from the main product has no weight, only a note.
decisions.why: Its sampling probability is kept with the draw, not on the row; an invented weight of 1 would bias every estimate built on it.

decisions.decision: The split strategy is a code, not a closed choice.
decisions.why: Each host names its strategies (group_disjoint there, time_group here).

decisions.decision: spec.objective maps to the metric point, and the main product's four ops points join the vocabulary.
decisions.why: Its objective is the primary metric with constraints; one shared vocabulary must hold every governed point.

change: dclab_core/ledger.py (new: POINTS, STATE_FIELDS, check_state, answer_problem, DecisionRecord, DecisionLabel), adapters/main_product_ledger.py (new), contracts.py, main_product_fields.json (semantic_decision_answers, vocabularies, Jev's bands and acting bands), schemas and baselines, CHANGELOG and 0.8.0, scripts/core_wheel_check.py; tests/test_ledger.py (new); CORE_INTEGRATION.md, CLAUDE.md, the plan and the roadmap.

findings.defect: The point vocabulary could not hold a problem decided on a draft here and on a project there.
findings.scenario: problem.ready from the main product's problem_spec_locked has a project subject.
findings.fix: A point names the subject kinds it accepts.

findings.defect: Split decisions from the main product were refused.
findings.scenario: holdout_strategy group_disjoint is not one of five choices.
findings.cause: The strategies were a closed choice of this studio's names.
findings.fix: The split point answers a code.

findings.scenario: A rule answer exclude with Jev at 0.95 came back as disagree, the row said agree.
findings.cause: The main product reads a leakage rule's words as a flag.
findings.fix: Read the rule's value as a flag, keep its words as raw, write them back.

findings.defect: An unavailable Jev answer came back as an abstention.
findings.cause: A model answer was always added.
findings.fix: No model answer when the row has none.

findings.defect: A score was treated as in band.
findings.scenario: proposal.completeness came back in band and disagreeing.
findings.fix: A score is never in band; its level stays as raw.

findings.defect: The policy outcome was lost on the way back.
findings.scenario: A review row and a classifier's answer both came back as rule.
findings.cause: used had no review and the outcome map defaulted to rule.
findings.fix: A review flag on the record; policy_outcome derived; unknown outcomes refused.

findings.defect: Label rows became duplicate decisions with labels pointing nowhere.
findings.scenario: A version-1 label produced a second record and supersedes a label id that never existed.
findings.cause: Label rows were read like answer rows.
findings.fix: A label row is a label of its chain's root; it supersedes only labels; a longer chain needs its rows.

findings.defect: Cell values could enter a record outside the state.
findings.scenario: Options and the value used accepted a person's name and 5000 characters.
findings.fix: Every answer, option and label checked against its point's answer shape.

findings.scenario: A split and an operating point got value_used accepted; a rejected promotion read as yes.
findings.cause: The adapter read a details.value no service writes, then the row's state.
findings.fix: Values from the facts each service writes; yes/no from type and state; none otherwise.

findings.defect: A blind label's weight was invented.
findings.cause: The row has no weight column.

findings.defect: The vocabulary missed governed points and mapped one wrongly.
findings.scenario: spec.objective was the family; the four ops points had no point.
findings.fix: Map spec.objective to the metric; add ops points; test both directions.

findings.defect: A model's answer could be used at level 0.
findings.scenario: A record at level 0 used a classifier: a row the main product never writes.
findings.cause: No check tied the level to the value used.
findings.fix: A model's answer is used only from level 2.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault in the contract and the adapter fails a test

measurements.name: main-product row shapes
measurements.gate: every recorded row shape comes back unchanged
measurements.result: identifier, leakage with the rule's words, unavailable, score, review and ai rows came back column for column
limits: Rows built from the recorded columns, not read from a live database.

outcome: One ledger holds decisions of both kinds from either host, in a state a decision model can train on without ever seeing a table's value, with labels that never invent what their source did not record.
lessons: Read the other host's writer, not only its schema: the values lived in facts, the weights with the draw, and the label rows in chains.
Check every field a record carries against what its point can answer, not only the obvious one.
risks: Counts and measures are aggregates by the caller's discipline.
A main-product answer's state is only a digest there until its side builds the bands.
